_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the fakefish playback/session constants.
Edit ONLY this file, then run `uv run fakefish-gen-constants`. That regenerates BOTH
firmware/eel_core/stim_levels.h   (C, consumed by the sketches)
src/fakefish/_constants.py        (Python, consumed by the toolchain)
and the CI gate asserts the regeneration leaves no git diff. Never hand-edit either
generated file — your edit will be silently reverted by the next codegen run.
NOT here on purpose:
* the SAMPLE RATE. It stays single-sourced in the export-generated eel_stimuli.h
(STIM_SAMPLE_RATE_HZ) / export_teensy_stimuli.PLAYBACK_RATE_HZ; the generated files
derive every sample-unit figure FROM it rather than restating it.
* StimKind. Already single-sourced in the export tool, which defines the Python STIM_*
values and emits the matching C enum.
* pins, thresholds, debounce, calibration. Those are per-surface (L3) or per-board (L1)
and live in firmware/eel_core/config.h or the sketch's own control header.
ONE MARKER CODE, AND ONLY THE SD DEVICE HAS IT.
sd_path.pulse_marker = 6 EOD pulses at a fixed 10 Hz with ALTERNATING polarity,
baked into the WAVs by build_sd_card.py. Identifies a playback.
Emitted as SD_MARKER_*.
The RC device's count-coded marker (rc_path.pulse_marker: 2 pulses = volley, 4 = sham,
at 100 Hz) was REMOVED on 2026-08-22 and PULSE_MARKER_* is gone with it. Two reasons.
It was redundant -- the per-pulse SD log is a precondition for output, so a trial and
its outcome are already on the card with a 20 us tick. And it was NOT redundant for a
sham, it was a stimulus: the no-stimulus control emitted four eel pulses before going
quiet, which is not a control. The SD device keeps its marker because it has no log at
all, so the lead-in is the only record that a playback happened -- the premise that
retired the RC one does not hold there.
The SD_MARKER_* prefix stays as it is. It was distinct to keep two codes apart and now
there is one, but renaming a shipped constant to celebrate a deletion is churn.
(History: the SD device used a 10 kHz SINE tone until 2026-08-17. It was removed because
the per-channel 2-pole output filter attenuates 10 kHz by ~21.8 dB, and because everything
the device emits should be made of eel pulses. See TODO.md.)
Consumed today by build_sd_card.py (Python), which BAKES these into the WAV card.
Also emitted to C as SD_* for a future live surface that renders these on-device.
Absolute output levels as a fraction of full scale (baked into the WAVs, NOT
peak-normalised).
LOCALIZATION IS A QUARTER OF THE VOLLEY, NOT A HALF (changed 2026-08-21, with the
fitted volley model). The synthetic volleys now carry the MEASURED within-volley
amplitude envelope, which decays ~22 % across a volley at the median and reaches
~0.34 of the volley's own peak at the 5th percentile. At the old 2:1 ratio the tail
of a decaying volley landed on top of the localization level, which is exactly the
separation that ratio existed to provide. Dropping localization to 1/4 restores it
without clipping the envelope: the retired alternative was a VOLLEY_DECAY_FLOOR
that flattened the measured decay on 64 % of volleys.
The absolute step between a volley and a resting discharge is NOT a measurement --
docs/VOLLEY_GENERATIVE_SPEC.md section 5 is explicit that it is confounded by
distance and clipping and must be treated as a knob. This is that knob.
The lead-in that identifies a playback: n_pulses EOD pulses at a FIXED rate with
ALTERNATING polarity, prepended to every B/C/D session.
Why this is detectable, and why each parameter is what it is:
* ALTERNATING polarity is the discriminator. No real eel alternates, and a
localization train is single-polarity, so the pattern cannot be confused with
biology or with the stimulus that follows it.
* Alternation also SURVIVES the firmware's per-press random polarity flip: the flip
negates the whole WAV, so the absolute sign is unpredictable but the alternation
is invariant. Detect the pattern, never the sign.
* n_pulses must be EVEN so the burst is CHARGE-BALANCED (equal numbers of each
polarity of an identical waveform => net charge ~0). This replaces the zero-sum
property the old sine LUT provided. The codegen asserts it.
* rate_hz sits BELOW the volley range (which peaks at 300-400 Hz) and the IPI stays
far longer than one EOD, so marker pulses never overlap.
Provisional values, easy to retune here: 6 pulses at 10 Hz.
Program A: a steady, single-polarity EOD train at a known rate and level — a plain
reference signal for setting gain and checking the rig. Single-polarity (unlike the
marker) so it is unambiguously a calibration signal and not a lead-in code; its net
charge is balanced across presses by the firmware's random polarity flip, exactly as
for the localization program.

session._comment: Session structure. Seconds/ms here; sample units are derived at codegen from the sample rate.

_comment: Consumed today by the RC sketch (C). NOMINAL levels only — on the 36 V DRV8871 stage
amplitude 1.0 means the full rail, so these are rail fractions, not volts.
BLINDED THREE-ARM TRIALS. The trigger fires in ONE direction only and does not say
which arm to run; the firmware draws the arm itself at the moment of playback. The
operator throws 'run a trial' and cannot choose what they deliver, so when and where
they fire cannot correlate with the arm — that correlation is the bias this removes.
THE THREE ARMS, and why there are three (2026-08-24). A two-arm volley-vs-nothing
design confounds 'a hunting discharge happened' with 'a fish is there at all'. The
question 'do volleys attract eels' needs a fish that is present and merely RESTING as
its own control, so the arms are:
VOLLEY   — a library discharge (the treatment)
BASELINE — resting-rhythm pulses at localization amplitude (fish present, not hunting)
SILENCE  — nothing at all (no fish)
ALL THREE LAST THE SAME LENGTH, drawn per trial from the volley library: every trial
picks a volley item, and VOLLEY plays it while BASELINE and SILENCE hold for exactly
its duration. The arms are therefore identical in duration distribution BY
CONSTRUCTION rather than by a matched constant that could drift. The old sham's length
was set by its LED animation (720 ms), which was longer than 80 % of the library's
volleys — the gap a sham left in the localization train was systematically longer than
the gap a volley left, so gap length alone leaked the arm.
THE BASELINE ARM ALWAYS EMITS ITS FIRST PULSE AT TRIAL ONSET. A volley's first pulse
is at t=0, so this is the correct parallel — but it is also load-bearing: at the
measured 3.15 Hz resting tick, an unanchored baseline arm of one volley-duration is
EMPTY in 40 % of trials (median 1 pulse), which would make two of the three arms
physically identical four times in ten. Anchored, the arm carries a mean of 2.6 pulses
and never zero. Do not remove the anchor.
weights are integer per-mille and MUST sum to exactly 1000 (gen_constants.validate
enforces it). 334/333/333 is the balanced design; 1000 cannot be divided three ways,
and a 0.1 % imbalance on one arm is far below any effect this experiment can resolve.
baseline_tick_hz / baseline_randomness are the treatment rhythm's OWN knobs and are
deliberately NOT the CH3/CH5 controls. The control condition is 'a resting eel', not
'a resting eel at whatever tempo the operator left the knob at' — and the arm has to
work with live localization switched fully off, which is exactly when CH3 reads REST.
3.15 Hz is LOC_NOMINAL_TICK_HZ, the measured animal; randomness 1.0 is the measured
eel and the top of CH5's range.
The draw happens in the sample-clock ISR, NOT in loop(), because random() is called
from the ISR elsewhere (polarity, the volley item pick) and must stay single-caller.
This blinds the arm END TO END. The LED shows ONE pattern for all three (see
TRIAL_LED_* in panel_control.h), so neither an observer on shore nor anyone scoring
the GoPro afterwards can read the arm off the device. The pulse log is the only
unblinding key.
The amplitude control sets the VOLLEY (max); localization is DERIVED as volley /
volley_amp_ratio (a quarter at 4.0). Anchoring at the volley keeps the ratio at every
pot position and needs no clamp. panel_volley_amp is the bench default with no transmitter.
4.0, not 2.0, since 2026-08-21: the synthetic volleys carry the measured amplitude
envelope, whose tail reaches ~0.34 of the volley's peak. At 2:1 that tail sat at the
localization level. Mirrors sd_path.levels.loc -- see the note there for the full
reasoning.
A quarter-scale pulse is comfortably above the driver's dead zone on the built
hardware: the bench A/B of 2026-08-22 showed the amplitude control works to the BOTTOM
of its travel with no compensation at all. The line that used to sit here credited the
OUT_PEDESTAL_DUTY offset for that; the pedestal was reverted the same day (it made the
output a cacophony and left both electrodes at ~3.1 V DC through every silence). See
firmware/eel_core/config.h -> 'The driver dead zone'.
Live localization train. Since 2026-08-21 its RHYTHM comes from a model fitted to
99 010 measured resting intervals (data/loc_model_params.json, vendored; see
docs/LOCALIZATION_GENERATIVE_SPEC.md and firmware/eel_core/loc_rhythm.h), not from
the unit-mean lognormal draw it used before. The model's own tables are NOT here --
they are generated into firmware/eel_core/loc_model_params.h from that JSON. Only
the KNOB RANGES the operator sees live here.
min_hz / max_hz are the CH3 throttle's ladder, and they are now a TICK TEMPO -- one
over the median interval, the number quoted as an eel's discharge rate -- because the
device anchors the median rather than the mean. The measured eel ticks at 3.15 Hz
(LOC_NOMINAL_TICK_HZ), with real single-fish slices spanning roughly 1.3-9.7 Hz.
THE LADDER IS LOGARITHMIC, and the range starts at 0.5 Hz. It was linear 1-20 Hz until
2026-08-22, which put ~85 % of the throttle's travel above anything a real eel does and
crammed the whole biological range into the bottom. Worse, 1 Hz sat inside the ~6 % of
travel between the 0.06 fail-safe cutoff and the 0.12 enable threshold -- so the slowest
settings were effectively unreachable, right against the edge where localization shuts
off. A field log (2026-08-22) bears it out: the operator never got below 4 Hz.
Geometric spacing fixes the resolution where it matters. Each of the RC_RATE_STEPS
rungs is a constant RATIO apart (~21 % at 20 steps over 0.5-20 Hz), so near 1 Hz the
steps are ~0.1 Hz rather than the old 1 Hz -- a ten-fold gain in low-rate control --
while the top of the range is unchanged. It also lands the measured eel at almost
exactly mid-throttle: sqrt(0.5 * 20) = 3.16 Hz against a nominal 3.153.
This is the change of meaning to watch: under the retired lognormal, a setting of
5 Hz meant 5 pulses per second on AVERAGE. It now means the fish ticks at 5 Hz, which
at panel_randomness 1.0 delivers about 3.3 pulses/s -- the interval distribution is
heavy-tailed, and one long silence eats half the average while contributing one
interval to the median. Spec section 5.3 has the full argument; knobs.gain_mean_anchor
in the model JSON is the table that would restore the old meaning.
panel_randomness is the bench default for CH5 (was panel_cv, a coefficient of
variation). 1.0 IS the measured eel: 0 is a metronome at the nominal tempo and the
knob is useful to about 1.5. It is not a jitter amount and does not blend toward a
Poisson process -- the lag-1 autocorrelation stays around 0.52 across the whole range.
refractory_samp is the minimum IPI. It MUST stay greater than EOD_HV_LEN so
localization pulses can never overlap -- that is what lets locgen use a single-pulse
scheduler instead of the overlap-add engine.
IT IS THE RESTING/VOLLEY ANTIMODE, NOT AN ARBITRARY SAFETY MARGIN. 1250 samples =
25 ms, taken from the fitted model's own provenance.resting_min_ipi_ms. It was 250
(5 ms) until 2026-08-21, and 5 ms sits squarely INSIDE volley territory.
Why that mattered once the rhythm became a model. The model's interval table is
clamped at the bottom to this same 25 ms antimode, precisely so the resting rhythm
can never intrude into volley territory (spec section 3). But that clamp lives in
SCORE space, while the rate knob is a pure TIME dilation -- so any CH3 setting above
the nominal 3.15 Hz tick scales the floor down with everything else. At CH3 = 10 Hz
the table's floor lands at 8.8 ms; at 20 Hz, 4.4 ms. The source analysis segments
resting pulses from fast runs on exactly this antimode, so those intervals would be
read as micro-bursts emitted by our own localization train -- contaminating the one
distinction the experiment rests on.
Re-imposing it in absolute time costs a visible spike at exactly 25 ms in a fast
train, which is the honest artifact: it says the device does not emit resting
intervals inside volley territory. This is a LOWER clamp and is not in tension with
leaving the long silences alone -- the spec clamps both ends of the table and defends
the bottom one in these terms. It engages on nothing at or below the nominal tempo.
synthetic_volleys.generate_localization applies the same floor to the SD items.
